It will be the first ESP.8 model deployed at Reyðarfjörður. Eimskip already operates two cranes of the same model at Sundahöfn, Reykjavík’s main cargo port, where they have been in service since 2024. This will allow Eimskip to operate the equipment using electricity from the local grid while retaining a diesel-powered option when required. candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%. candidates.title: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom
candidates.excerpt: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom Private credit is gaining ground in Asia as demand for flexible capital grows and the AI boom needs funding, according to KKR. Asia has historically relied on banks for credit, and they still provide 88 per cent of the region’s debt capital, compared with 50 per cent in Europe and just 31 per cent in the US. However, forces reshaping Japan and driving investment in AI infrastructure are starting to change this, KKR said in a recent blog post. In the US and Europe, regulators have made banks retrench, but that is not happening in Asia. Instead, private credit is in demand across the region because it offers flexible capital alongside banks that remain deeply embedded in corporate financing. KKR argued that Asian banks provide cheap but inflexible capital, and that private credit was plugging this gap. The Amsterdam-based fintech business, which serves 300,000 businesses, has introduced a business overdraft and credit card, offering personalised limits of up to €20,000 (£16,700) and €40,000, respectively. The products use customers’ existing transaction data to make credit decisions in seconds, removing the need for businesses to submit annual accounts or bank statements. Finom said more than half of its customers now qualify for credit under the new offering, compared with between 11 per cent and 17 per cent under its previous credit product. candidates.excerpt: Two men were arrested after a shooting involving Union Pacific Railroad Police investigating suspected cargo theft near the busy Tehachapi Loop on Nov. 12. Railroad (NYSE: UNP) police were patrolling the area in response to recent thefts from trains when they discovered an open cargo-container door, authorities said. Officers began investigating, and a shooting occurred, according to the sheriff’s account. A suspect fled on foot, and railroad police secured the area and requested assistance from the sheriff’s office. Kern County detectives responded and took over the investigation. Investigators subsequently located Jesus Rodriguez, 32, in Keene and arrested him.
